recall.question: B1: Write the pretraining loss and name the two phases.
recall.answer: L_pre(theta) = (1/n) sum_i l_pre(x^(i), theta). Phases: pretraining on broad (usually unlabeled) data, then adaptation to downstream tasks.

recall.question: B3: Write the LoRA update, its scaling, and its trainable parameter count.
recall.answer: Delta W = B A, B in R^{d_out x r}, A in R^{r x d_in}, h = W_0 x + (alpha / r) B A x. Trainable count r(d_out + d_in).

recall.question: B6: Define Recall@k and NDCG@k.
recall.answer: Recall@k = |R(q) intersect top-k| / |R(q)|, NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k with logarithmic discount. Recall@k ignores ranking.

keyTerms.definition: Write (15.2) and (15.3); state the initialization of each.
The probe is convex quadratic; finetuning is nonconvex.

recall.question: D1.3: Why does the probe have a closed form?
recall.answer: The probe is linear in w with squared loss: a convex quadratic with the normal-equation closed form. Finetuning optimizes a nonconvex neural loss with no closed form.

recall.question: D2.2: Report the SIMCLR toy numbers.
D2.3: Why does the loss pull positives together?
recall.answer: -log(p/(p+q)) has negative derivative in p and positive in q; p = exp(positive inner product), q = sum of exp(negative inner products).

keyTerms.definition: -log(p/(p+q)) decreases in p, increases in q for p, q > 0.
Recall@3, DCG@5, IDCG@5, NDCG@5 on the given ranking.

recall.question: Q1: Prove the SIMCLR scalar monotonicity.
recall.answer: f = -log p + log(p + q). df/dp = -q/(p(p+q)) < 0. df/dq = 1/(p+q) > 0. Holds for p, q > 0.

keyTerms.definition: The denominator must sum j != i, not all j.
Embeddings must be normalized first.

recall.question: T1: Identify the two bugs in the SIMCLR code.
recall.answer: Bug 1: the denominator sums over all j including i; the notes' variant sums j != i. Bug 2: embeddings are not normalized. Check: moving each positive pair closer must lower the loss.

keyTerms.definition: HNSW, quantization, or inverted-file indexes for 2B documents.
Image-text pairs: positives are the paired views.

recall.question: S1: How do you serve 2B documents under 50 ms?
recall.answer: Use an approximate nearest-neighbor index: HNSW graph search, quantization, or inverted-file/centroid indexes. Monitor index recall against brute force and tail latency.

recall.question: S2: Redefine the pairs for image-text data.
recall.answer: Positive pair: the image and its paired text. Negatives: the image with other items' texts (and symmetrically).

recall.answer: Hidden condition: the 40 tasks are all near the pretraining distribution, where a low-rank update has enough capacity. It fails under large shifts or high-rank changes.
